# 1 Enoch Chapter 39 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 39:2 — "books of indignation and wrath" vs. "books filled with wrath and anger"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "books of-indignation and-wrath" | Literal compound noun pairs |
| LOGOS | "books of indignation and wrath" | Same, without hyphens |
| PNEUMA | "books filled with wrath and anger" | Paraphrase; adds "filled with" for readability |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Books of indignation and wrath" (LOGOS). PNEUMA's "filled with" adds an element absent from the Ge'ez. "Indignation" and "wrath" are distinct terms deserving preservation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 39:3 — "whirlwind" vs. "storm-wind" vs. "great wind"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "storm-wind" | Compound preserving Ge'ez construct |
| LOGOS | "whirlwind" | More natural English; evokes Elijah (2 Kgs 2:11) |
| PNEUMA | "great wind" | Simplified |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Whirlwind" (LOGOS). The Elijah allusion is appropriate — Enoch's ascent mirrors Elijah's. "Great wind" (PNEUMA) loses specificity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 39:10 — "those who sleep not" — identity

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those-who-sleep-not" | Literal; angelic beings who never rest |
| LOGOS | "those who sleep not" | Formal; same reference |
| PNEUMA | "Those who never sleep" | Same meaning, more natural phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Those who sleep not" (LOGOS). The archaic inversion ("sleep not") is warranted here as it echoes the liturgical register of the passage and connects to Rev 4:8 ("they rest not day and night").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS, acknowledging PNEUMA's naturalness.

---

## 39:13 — "thousands of thousands / ten thousand times ten thousand" vs. "thousands upon thousands"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "thousands-of-thousands and-ten-thousand-times-ten-thousand" | Literal pair, full Ge'ez idiom |
| LOGOS | "thousands upon thousands, ten thousand upon ten thousand" | Formal; uses English reduplication idiom |
| PNEUMA | "thousands of thousands, tens of thousands of tens of thousands" | Natural English pattern |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Thousands upon thousands, ten thousand upon ten thousand" (LOGOS). The "upon" construction conveys accumulation well. All renderings are equivalent; LOGOS is most elegant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements: 4**
